newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW-Australia wheat exports near target.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW-Australia wheat exports near target.

text.p: Australia is about two-thirds of the way to its target of exporting 17 million tonnes of wheat in the 1996/97 marketing year ending September 30, an Australian Wheat Board (AWB) official said on Monday.
The AWB has so far made sales and secured commitments for about 11 million tonnes of wheat for the year, Nigel Officer, manager of the AWB's international division, told Reuters.
Officer said an aggressive marketing programme overseas had helped move Australian wheat into overseas markets in a year that saw a record crop estimated at 23 million tonnes.
"We've been very succesful in our marketing," Officer said.

The latest sale saw the AWB sell 200,000 tonnes of Australian Standard White wheat to India for March delivery at around US$186 a tonne, significantly above the AWB pool price estimate of A$193 a tonne.
The sale increased Australia's sales to India to 1.3 million tonnes in the current season, more than three-quarters of the total 1.7 million tonnes India has purchased this year, Officer said.
However, the number of tender opportunities may be waning due to international buyers turning to domestic crop expectations as the northern season approaches, Officer said.
"We've been very active, but the number of tenders now seems to be thinning out," Officer said.
Pakistan is expected at some point to tender internationally for up to 270,000 tonnes of wheat for April delivery.
But beyond that, the AWB official said it is mostly "regular business" for exports, Officer said.
